To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the joint provision of audit services by accounting firms is positively related to the size of the firm, and is negatively related to its leverage and the extent of institutional holdings.
companies that face high agency costs purchase less nonaudit services from their audiors.

(1) companies with higher agency costs proxies (i.e. higher leverage ratios, lower profitability ratios, higher growth ratios and higher institutional shareholdings) purchase relatively smaller amounts (in absolute terms) of non-audit from their auditors; and (2) companies with higher audit fees purchase relatively larger amounts of non-auditing services from their auditor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a phenomenon that is of increasing importance to accounting firms, audit regulators, and investors.
the joint provision of audit services and non-audit consulting by accounting firms.
the joint provision of audit services by accounting firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the joint provision of audit services and consultancy services does not appear to be a significant factor in the provision of non-audit consultancy services to clients.

the provision of non-audit and audit services are not substitutes but complements, and the provision of nonaudit and audit services are complementary in the sense that a firm that purchases non-audit services is also more likely to purchase audit services.
there is a negative relationship between the provision of non-audit service and the provision of audit service.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are agency costs in the joint provision of audit/non-audit services and that the provision of non-audit and audit services is a strategic decision.
the provision of non-audit consultancy services by the audit firms to their audit client is associated with the agency costs proxies.
companies facing potentially high agency costs are associated with smaller amounts of nonaudit fees paid to the company's auditor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the provision of non-audit and audit services is not necessarily a zero-sum game.
there are significant differences in the joint provision of audit services and other services by auditors.
companies facing high levels of agency costs are associated with lower levels of joint audit and non-auditing services.
